content:
carmen: Heads up — us-west inference fleet hit sustained GPU saturation ~08:05 UTC. Queue length spiked to ~17k, p95 gen latency >5s, some 503s. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/xyz :grimacing:
ops-bot: Incident created: gpu-utilization-high (us-west) — paging @sre-oncall :rotating_light:
jake: seeing it. Admission controller shows soft-admit at 100% and backlog keeps growing. Any recent deploys?
priya: no deploys in last 30m. Networking metrics: increased packet drops between gw1 -> gpu-pool, container start times jumped from 150ms -> 1.8s.
marta: immediate mitigation: lower burst tokens and enable fallback model route for non-SLA traffic. Can someone flip admission? :pray:
kevin: doing quick change now. Pushing adm config tweak:
```bash
# reduce burst for us-west token-bucket
curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/admission/us-west -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"burst_size":200, "refill_rate":50}'
```
kevin: also adding a temporary small-model route for best-effort traffic:
```json
{"route_filter":{"priority":"best-effort"}, "model":"redwood-small-fallback"}
```
jake: added route. Non-SLA traffic should see fallback within 30s.
priya: enabling extra prewarm nodes (+10) for 10m to cut cold start latency and turning on hedging for 30s. Command: `infractl prewarm add --pool us-west --count 10 --ttl 600`
marta: queue length down after ~2m, p95 now ~1.2s. Good short-term signal but cost will rise if we keep prewarm up. :money_with_wings:
carmen: thanks. We need a long-term approach: adaptive prewarm driven by short-term demand forecast + queue-derived soft-admit with hysteresis. Also enforce per-customer emergency caps when backlog > threshold.
kevin: noted. Also spotted provider errors when provisioning new GPU nodes — looks like the cloud API started returning 429s for instance create (quota or rate-limit). That explains slow replenishment.
priya: propose pattern: predictive scaler (EWMA over 5m) -> schedule warm nodes with buffer; pair with soft-admit that only decays when queue < Q_low for Y seconds to avoid oscillation. Add a per-model concurrency cap to shard load.
marta: agree. Also include a "cost tolerance" param so teams can trade SLO vs spend per workload. We'll need a short RFC + runbook for oncall.
kevin: I'll draft RFC and runbook in eng-infra, include a simulation notebook for cost vs SLO. Assigning to @jake @priya for modelling.
jake: also want to test token-bucket per-region + per-customer bucket to isolate noisy tenants. Small canary rollout first.
sre-oncall: monitoring note: added dashboard with queue/arrival-rate/EWMA forecast + provisioning lag. Watch for 10m horizon drift.
carmen: for now keep throttles tightened and prewarm window to 10m. Postmortem/RFC timeline: RFC this week, runbook next week. Thanks all :thumbsup:
